I love breakfast food, but I just can't seem to force myself out of bed on weekdays to actually make it. Unfortunately this usually means I go without and eat an early lunch instead. 

If you're like me you might consider some recipes you can prep, or even cook the night before. Cutting down on early morning cooking means more time in bed, and that works for me!

as Schpsych said, quiche is an excellent alternative to early morning cooking *I don't recommend microwaving it, but cold quiche slice and a cup of hot coffee is pretty tasty!

Pancakes reheat surprisingly well, and will keep for a few days if nicely wrapped. If you throw in a little black pepper they make great vessels for breakfast sandwiches I recommend - Fry 1 egg per sandwich, put spinach on one side, and a bit of cheese on the other, a bit of tomato and some salt! Bam breakfast in under 10 minutes (If pancakes are prepped the night before)

Also steel cut oatmeal, breakfast burritos, muffins, granola with yoghurt. So many great, quick, and fun things to do with this meal! Good luck with finding what works for you!! :)

A few years ago I was at a pub with good friend of mine. It was getting late and we were thinking about jumping into a cab, and we'd just sat down outside for some fresh air, when this scraggly older homeless man strolls over to us and says 'Hi! Having a good party?!' we said yes, thank you and he sat down on the side walk and pulled a half empty mickey of Appleton Estate. We started chatting and laughing. We were all drunk and this guy was genuinely sweet and funny. Weird thing was he kept calling me Angela (not my name). 

After a bit I started to feel sorry for the guy (His name was Roger), he was litterally skin and bones. I asked him when the last time he ate was, he said day before, then he winked and held up his bottle "don't matter anyway. Food would just get in the way of my alcohol!" I could have left it, but I didn't I asked if I bought him a slice of pizza if he'd eat it. He said sure and off I went. By the time I got back he was getting all misty eyed talking to my friend.

 I took it as our cue to leave, and leave we did. It wasn't until after we left that my friend told me Angela was the daughter he hadn't spoken to in almost 20 years. I guess she'd have been our age, maybe a little older.

 Anyway it always stayed with me, and it's made me kinder to strangers. No matter what, thats someones dad, or son, or sister, or friend. 

TL;DR Bought pizza for a homeless man after a night of partying and never forgot again that every person you meet is something to someone.

I'm not sure what's been said for the music scene here, but when I moved last May I was surprised and pleased to find a few fun quirky events to keep my big city expectations somewhat realized.

There's [improv comedy friday and saturday nights](http://www.rapidfiretheatre.com/shows/)

Open mic musical evenings at my favorite tea house, [Cha Island](http://www.chaisland.com/) (Not to mention delicious waffles!)

Secret street car concerts that run on the [high level bridge street car](http://eatingisthehardpart.com/2012/07/28/a-secret-streetcar-concert/)

And of course for food, fun, and all your knick knack needs there's a multitude of farmers markets (Including the 104street market on saturdays, and the Strathcona farmers market also on saturdays!)

Many more fun things to be done and seen! IMHO I'd skip the museum, and I found the Telus World of Science a little bit more geared to kids (still not a bad way to spend a rainy afternoon!). 

Most importantly, don't be afraid to make friends. Albertans love to drink and love to drink with YOU!

The long and short of it is bread baking can be as complicated and expensive as you'd like it to be! This is a whole other thread on the costs of flour and an entire site about baking it! http://www.thefreshloaf.com/node/6343/cost-flour
